This is a submerse for a game dedicated to predicting the future.

The scoreboard is here: invisibleprophet.com

The rules are

  1. No predictions for petty crime will be admissible

  2. If a news publication shows the prediction was made after the event, the prediction will be void

  3. Each week in advance that a prediction is made will count for one prediction. This means that if you get the prediction right three weeks in advance you will get 3/3 added to your ratio.

  4. However, if you get it wrong, you will get 0/3 added to your ratio.

  5. Prediction will be voided if it has already been reported in a news publication (editorials or opinion pieces are ok)

  6. If participant participated in predicted event, it is void

  7. You can simply agree with someone else's prediction to gain points, but you must clearly state that you want to add their prediction to your ratio

  8. This is a fluid game, and whether predictions are significant enough to count towards points will be somewhat subjective. In other words, don't make stupid predictions about a car accident in the USA on July 15th, 2015. That is too broad and will be ignored. HOWEVER, you will be told it has been ignored and you are free to argue your case on the board.

How to Play

  1. Create or post in a thread with a prediction of something that will be reported in the news in the future

  2. State the who, what, where, when, and why of your prediction

  3. The "what" and the "when" will determine the accuracy of your prediction

  4. Every prediction you make will count as one prediction, every correct prediction you make will give you one point

  5. The amount of points you earned compared to the amount of predictions you have made will create your ratio or percentile (points earned/predictions made = your score)

  6. Your rank will be determined by your ratio or percentile.

  7. You must make 10 predictions to be placed on the scoreboard, these predictions will count towards your ratio

State of the Image Host - 50 Day of Shitlording & Contest annoucement

Introduction

Hello, for those who don't know I'm Technician90, the creator of Slimgur, originally I created it as a response to the censorship of FPH content on imgur. It's been 50 days since I launched Slimgur and It's been a lot of fun and a learning experience. We are currently hosting over 32 000 images, 1 250 albums with 2 300 registered users. I've made this post to discuss planned features and bug fixes for the upcoming months and to answer any other questions you may have.

Commenting System

After a lot of searching for a commenting system that addresses all the needs of the site I've settled on Hashover, It offers all the features that I want in a commenting system, like the ability to vote comments up or down, nested replies and anonymous posting. Most importantly I chose Hashover because comments are hosted on the Slimgur webserver, which means that the comments and IP addresses aren't being logged by a third party company (such as Discus or Livefyre). Also I would like to thank Jacob Barkdull, the developer of Hashover for his work in helping me implement Hashover on my site. The bug where the comments were redirecting to a blank page is fixed. This changeover means that any old comments have been deleted, but I trust that you'll have no problem filling it back up.

Future Features

We've had a lot of requests for features, and I want to make sure that Slimgur remains the shitlord image host of choice, here are a list of the planned features that I hope to implement over the next month or so.

  • Ctrl+V Uploading
  • Integration of user accounts with commenting system
  • Private uploads for users without accounts
  • Albums for users without accounts
  • Better sorting method for large albums
  • Extensions for Firefox and Safari

If you have any thoughts for additional features, feel free to post it here in this thread or if you think of it later on the Slimgur subverse

Bugs

There have been some problems using the site, I want to address those as quickly as possible, so far the two biggest ones are:

  • Mobile Zoom issues
  • Random Image Resizing

Removal of the Explore section

I've be thinking about taking the explore section down on Slimgur. After getting the analyitics it only accounts for a small portion of the traffic and would go a long way to making things more secure. Without the explore section all uploads would be private as no users would be able to browse through all the images.

Let me know what you think about this in the comments below.

Top Image Contest

I was thinking that this would be a nice way to give back to the community. I'm sure you noticed the new trophy icon in the top bar of Slimgur. Each day around midnight whatever image has the most views for the day will be featured the next day in the "yesterday's top image" section.

Unfortunately only images that use viewer links (as opposed to direct links) can be considered, as the code used to determine top images is part of the viewer page. Links to albums are also counted and can win the contest.

At the end of the month I will randomly draw one of the month's top images and send them some Slimgur Swag. Basically all my traffic comes from voat, so if it's uploaded with an anonymous account or a fake email (which is fine) then after announcing the winner the user can contact me and I'll check their submission history on voat. The first draw will be the end of July, I only started logging traffic two days ago, so your odds for this month are 1 in 5 if your submission is a top image this month.

Thank you!

Thanks for all your continued support, you guys are the best! I'll be hanging out in the comments section for a couple of hours to answer any questions or comments.

The community itself will grow over time. A percentage of the photos are not FPH, a percentage of those viewers will comment and slowly build the community, comment by comment. I like to think I have possible ideas, but it is one thing to think of an idea, it is another for the idea to be accepted (even if it is reasonable).

Inform the userbase of the change, make the change, and measure your criteria and the community's thoughts.

On top of this you (will) have issues occurring that you don't know about, unknown unknowns. It should be smoother with proper focus and an understanding that you need to help the community grow as that could damage the site's foundation (See: Reddit June 2015 - July 2015).

Also your site is awesome, the community appreciates your work, even if there are times you don't feel that way.

Finances

The google adsense money has given me enough to cover 2 months of hosting fees, it was just very unreliable on a day to day basis and I wanted to try other ad networks. It's nice to know that I can go back to adsense and at least make enough to cover costs if this network doesn't pan out. I am paying month to month, because we grew so quickly in the beginning I wasn't sure what hosting tier was going to be the best and as it becomes more popular I may need to change it the future.

Bandwidth

Bandwidth is unlimited with this hosting plan so there is no cost between a direct link vs a viewer link. The only thing is that a direct link will not generate any comments and it will not generate any ad revenue. So its neutral, not negative. This will change if I sign up with a content delivery network which will speed up loading times and I plan to do once Slimgur is more financially stable.

Community

So part of the reason I like Slimgur is that using it as an image host sort of sends a message about the user. The FPH community has always been really proud about their status and membership and I think the main reason Slimgur is so successful is because of its strong and visible connection to the FPH community. I don't want to sever or downplay that connection at all. I hope one day to see a merciless shitlord commenting community throughout my site. As for the name of the community members, I think that will come up naturally if it reaches a certain size.

Explore page

I like the idea of a "trending" section instead of an explore section. Maybe the answer isn't to get rid of the explore section but to change the way it works.

everything else

I promise I will continue to do my best in informing everyone of changes, getting feedback and maintaining the connection with the userbase. I really like being a participant in this community and doing these "state of the image host" posts are one of my favorite parts.

There will always be unknown unknowns, that's just the nature of the internet, I'm confident that Slimgur will be able to face the challenges that will arise as it grows.

Through the whole story, quite the big deal is made about how terrible the unforgivable curses are. It's literally right in the name, that they are an irredeemable step towards the darkness. That using them is not just a sign of how serious you are, but that you have to tap into something terrible and really mean it to effectively use them.

And then, the closer you get to the end, the more freely the protagonists use them. And not just in secret, not just out of desperation. No, at the final battle, they're being thrown around freely by good and bad alike, and used effectively by both sides as well.

Was I the only one disappointed that this is what it came to? That they never found an effective alternative, or repurposed something unexpected, rather than sinking to that level? And no one ever points any of this out, there's no consequences for using this forbidden magic.No one seems horrified, no one seems to regret it.
The Unforgivable Curses in The Deathly Hallows

Interesting perspective! I actually really appreciated the realistic (or as realistic as you can get in a magical universe) portrayal of how far the protagonists were willing to go to win the war. It's kind of like the Batman thing: because Batman vows never to kill anyone, if he must kill someone to defeat the villain, it's especially powerful. Know what I mean?

Its usage also suggests that the "good guys" that we are rooting for aren't so black-and-white good, after all. They're human, with human flaws, and perhaps the best you can say is that they're less evil than the bad guys. Tack on the way the Ministry dealt with the bad guys (arresting Stan Shunpike, etc), and you have a really interesting political situation ripe for awesome fanfiction.

Also, I loved Harry's attempt at Crucio-ing Bellatrix in the fifth book. It reflected his mental state really well.

I think I'd be more inclined to see it that way, if that's what it all came down to. If Harry had to use one to finish off Voldemort, or if one of the other characters had used one as a last resort... but there's no agonizing over it, no shock or horror that they were used. Harry gets in a lot more trouble for Sectumsempra than anyone does for an unforgivable. For that matter, it disappointed me that Sectumsempra never really came back after the end of HBP.

Fair point :) I feel like at some point we must accept that JK Rowling's books aren't perfect. Why did Sectumsempra disappear? The Time Turner/Room of Requirement were both super OP, why didn't the characters use them like crazy? Why does JK Rowling go through the trouble of making an evil Gryffindor (Peter Pettigrew) and a non-evil Slytherin (Snape), only to treat all Slytherins as lesser and evil throughout the whole series?

It's definitely a fascinating universe though. :)
